financial_checks.claim: $50,000 new car at "$600 per month"; $35,000 after 12 months; $15,000 depreciation
financial_checks.result: $35,000 is 30% depreciation ($15,000) and holds; a $50,000 loan at 7% over 60 months is about $990/month, and $600 matches about $30,000 financed at 7% over 60 months; loan terms, down payment or trade-in are not stated.

financial_checks.claim: A dollar at 35 is worth four times a dollar at 55 by age 65
financial_checks.result: 1.08^20 = 4.66 (3.87 at 7%); "four times" is roughly right and conservative at 8%.

financial_checks.claim: Delaying a $15,000 roof repair leads to $40,000 of water damage, "three times as much"
financial_checks.result: 2.67x; and the earlier roof check is $18,000, not $15,000 (unreconciled).

financial_checks.claim: Ramsey Solutions study of more than 10,000 millionaires
financial_checks.result: Exists (over 10,000 US millionaires, fielded Nov 2017-Jan 2018 per Ramsey; 79% reported no inheritance). The video's grocery-spending and "Hondas and Toyotas" statements were not located.

financial_checks.claim: Rich Habits study: 92% no luxury cars, 97% never leased, 55% buy used
financial_checks.result: Five-year study of 233 wealthy people (177 self-made) confirmed from secondary summaries; the three percentages were not found. Small, self-reported sample.

financial_checks.claim: Goldman Sachs: missing the 10 best days since 2009 cuts returns from ~17% to ~12%; Nasdaq -78% in the dot-com crash; neighbours of lottery winners file for bankruptcy more; luxury brands charge "40 times the manufacturing cost"
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified. The 40x figure is presented as a statistic with no source and reads as hyperbole.

strengths: Strong frame story with a clean callback.
Concrete, actionable rules (24-hour / 7-day / 30-day pauses; route half of every raise to savings first).
Plain analogies for lifestyle inflation and time value.
Delivers exactly the nine promised signs.
weaknesses: Several attributed statistics have no locatable source and are presented with false precision.
Car-payment premise does not reconcile with a $50,000 purchase.
Intro promise that the signs apply at any income is contradicted by wealth-dependent signs.
Like/subscribe ask before any value; unclear end instruction.
contradictions: "No matter what your current income is" versus sign 7 requiring a $3M portfolio.
improvement_opportunities: State the car-loan terms or use $990/month so the $600/month and $900,000 figures reconcile on screen.
Replace attributed percentages with figures that can be cited (the Ramsey study) or label them "survey of 233 people".
Reword the intro promise to "most signs apply at any income; two need real capital".
Move the first subscribe ask after sign one or two and replace "don't click on it just yet" with one explicit next-video instruction.
unavailable: Original source documents for Rich Habits percentages and the Goldman figure
